business_model.claim: SPH manages its operations in four segments—Propane, Fuel Oil and Refined Fuels, Natural Gas and Electricity, and All Other—of which three are reportable; Propane is by far the largest, with nine-month 2026 revenues of $1,044,492 thousand versus $62,244 thousand for Fuel Oil and Refined Fuels.

business_model.basis: Stated in 10-K MD&A and Item 1 Business.
business_model.claim: Profitability is driven by the spread between the retail selling price and the cost to acquire and transport product; propane supply is purchased from approximately 45 wholesalers at approximately 140 supply points under one-year agreements priced off posted prices at major storage points such as Mont Belvieu, Texas.
quotes: The level of profitability in the retail propane, fuel oil, natural gas and electricity businesses is largely dependent on the difference between retail sales price and our costs to acquire and transport products.
Our propane supply is purchased from approximately 45 wholesalers at approximately 140 supply points located throughout the United States and Canada.

Our propane supply contracts typically provide for pricing based upon index formulas using the posted prices established at major supply points such as Mont Belvieu, Texas, or Conway, Kansas (plus transportation costs) at the time of delivery.

business_model.basis: Stated in both 10-K and 10-Q MD&A; confirmed by the actual Q3 2026 net loss in the income statement.
business_model.claim: Revenue is highly seasonal: approximately two-thirds of retail propane volume and approximately three-fourths of retail fuel oil volume are sold during the October-through-March heating season, producing a typical net loss in the third fiscal quarter (April–June).
quotes: Historically, approximately two-thirds of our retail propane volume is sold during the six-month peak heating season from October through March.
Consistent with the seasonal nature of our business, we typically experience a net loss in the third quarter of our fiscal year.
Net loss for the third quarter of fiscal 2026 was $17.5 million, or $0.26 per Common Unit

business_model.basis: Stated in 10-Q MD&A and 8-K earnings release; the 10-K provides multi-year weather context.
business_model.claim: Weather is a primary revenue driver: warmer-than-normal temperatures reduce heating demand and volumes; in Q3 fiscal 2026, average temperatures were 17% warmer than normal, contributing to a 1.8% decline in propane gallons sold to 70.6 million gallons.
quotes: Retail propane gallons sold in the third quarter of fiscal 2026 of 70.6 million gallons decreased 1.8% compared to the prior year third quarter, primarily due to warmer spring temperatures that adversely impacted heat-related demand.

Average temperatures (as measured by heating degree days) across all of the Partnership's service territories during the third quarter of fiscal 2026 were 17% warmer than normal and 3% warmer than the prior year third quarter.

business_model.claim: Commodity price levels drive both revenue and cost of products sold: average wholesale propane costs for fiscal 2025 were 5.8% higher than the prior year, and average posted propane prices for Q3 fiscal 2026 increased 3.6% year-over-year due to geopolitical tensions and export demand.
quotes: During fiscal 2025, the wholesale cost of propane generally trended higher than the prior year during the first nine months of the year, and then turned lower during the fourth quarter, resulting in average wholesale costs for the full year being 5.8% higher than the prior year.

average posted propane prices for the third quarter of fiscal 2026 increased 3.6% (basis Mont Belvieu, Texas) compared to the prior year third quarter due to geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and strong export demand.

business_model.claim: Operating and G&A expenses rose in Q3 fiscal 2026 to $141.4 million, up 3.8% year-over-year, driven by higher payroll, fuel and vehicle maintenance costs, partially offset by lower variable compensation and a benefit from RNG production tax credits.
quotes: Combined operating and general and administrative expenses were $141.4 million for the third quarter of fiscal 2026, an increase of $5.2 million, or 3.8%, compared to the prior year third quarter.

The increase was primarily attributable to higher payroll and benefit-related expenses and increased fuel and vehicle maintenance costs, partially offset by lower variable compensation costs and a benefit from production tax credits earned during the current-year quarter from RNG production.
